data.name: Ayanyak
data.long_meaning: Ayanyak is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'Aya' meaning 'lord' and 'Nyak' meaning 'sacred' or 'pure'. This name is used to denote someone who is the lord or protector of the sacred. In Hindu mythology, Ayanyak is an epithet for various deities, particularly Lord Vishnu and Lord Ganesha, who are revered as the protectors of the dharma or righteous path.
data.spiritual_meaning: Protector of the sacred and dharma.

historical_references.reference: Ayanyak, also known as Yayati, was a legendary king in Hindu mythology, the father of the Pandavas and the ancestor of the Kurus. He is said to have ruled around 3219 BCE.
historical_references.context: Legendary king and ancestor of the Kurus and Pandavas.

historical_references.reference: Ayanyak, or Yayati, is also mentioned in the Mahabharata as a powerful king who renounced his kingdom and underwent the curse of age, living out his remaining years as a wandering ascetic. This occurred around 3136 BCE.
historical_references.context: Renounced his kingdom and lived out his remaining years as a wandering ascetic.
